runs.content: Thursday's rotation focus is Books + Podcasts. Since the last thinker run (2026-09-02), log.md shows only two events: a routine MDT paper-trade entry and today's podcast-recommender run, which generated 4 new suggestions (Exponential View, The Matt Walker Podcast, Sound School Podcast, Circles Off). Books had no new activity — book-summarizer runs monthly and last fired 2026-09-01. The deep-dive centred on the fresh podcast batch, cross-checked against the full wiki map. Two genuinely new, non-duplicate finds: (1) Exponential View (Azeem Azhar) is pitched explicitly as an economist/policy voice — Fred's now-deep AI podcast list skews toward researchers, engineers, and operators, with nobody covering 'institutional and labour-market effects at a societal level.' [[ai-tech/ai-future-of-work]]'s own 'Institutional Gap' section is built entirely around this exact framing ('AI is moving at technology speed; institutions move at political speed') and its Open Questions section still asks, unresolved since May, whether any policy response actually works — a standing supply-side source for a question the page has only had one demand-side data point against (Gates' token tax, logged 2026-08-30). (2) Sound School Podcast is the first recommendation aimed at audio production itself — sound design, tape editing, pacing for the ear — explicitly distinguished by its own pitch from the two prior prose/screenwriting recommendations (Scriptnotes, Writing Excuses). [[lightfin/inspiration-authors]] covers six prose authors in depth but has zero content on audio-drama production craft, despite Lightfin Casefiles being a radio-play podcast, not a book — sharpening the still-open 2026-07-16 Scriptnotes idea, which never got past prose/screenwriting either. No new investigation idea cleared the bar today (Circles Off and The Matt Walker Podcast both repeat already-logged recommender patterns for Sports Betting and Health respectively), and nothing in the existing open sections showed signs of resolution — book-breath.md and health/source-godin-breathwork-2026.md, flagged 2026-09-01, still don't cross-link each other.

Wednesday's rotation focus is Health + Learning. Since the last thinker run (2026-09-01), log.md shows zero new activity of any kind — no trades, no clippings, no new pages in any domain. Health's pages (overview, my-protocol, the two source pages) are unchanged since May, so the deep-dive turned to Learning's framework pages and person-seth-godin.md, cross-checked against the full wiki map for connections outside today's pair. Two genuinely new, non-duplicate finds: (1) Buffett's 'concentrate your effort and ruthlessly avoid the rest' principle is written down three separate times in the wiki with no cross-links — [[finance/ideas/idea-berkshire-principles]]'s Principle 5 ('A Few Winners to Work Wonders,' synthesised from four Berkshire letters), [[learning/source-buffett-525-rule]]'s sharper 'Avoid-At-All-Cost list' framing from an unrelated career-advice anecdote about Buffett and his pilot, and [[learning/altmba-freds-work]]'s own P12 breakthrough ('Mediocre is OK') where Fred independently arrived at the identical insight about his own career in 2018. (2) [[learning/framework-abn-analysis]]'s whole diagnostic method — is a boundary self-imposed/narrative or genuinely real/structural? — maps directly onto the actual structure of disagreement in [[work/source-workday-disruption-debate-2026]]: a16z's Schmidt treats Workday's moat as self-imposed and breakable by AI agents, while LaRocque and Turnbull argue the real boundary is regulatory/structural (compliance accountability, config framework). ABN's own Cross-References table lists Finance, Crypto, Games and Lightfin as domains to apply it to but omits Work entirely, and neither page cites the other. No new investigation idea cleared the bar today — Health and Learning's pages were checked against the existing Open Investigation Ideas list and turned up nothing not already logged — and nothing in the existing open sections showed signs of resolution.
